name: Lithuania

income_tax.summary: From 1 Jan 2026 most income is aggregated: 20% up to 36 average wages (EUR 83,237.40), 25% to 60 average wages (EUR 138,729), 32% above; some income is taxed at a flat 15%. NPD (non-taxable allowance): maximum EUR 747 a month at pay up to the EUR 1,153 minimum wage, reduced by 0.49 x (income - minimum wage), ending at EUR 2,677.49 a month; not modelled (personal_allowance 0). Employee social security 19.5% including 6.98% health, withheld; above 60 average wages (EUR 138,729) only the 6.98% health applies (recorded cap EUR 138,729 for the capped part).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Recorded 17.55% is the effective rate on income: 19.5% (including 6.98% health) levied on 90% of individual-activity income; the cap is the EUR 99,422 base ceiling (43 average wages) expressed as income (99,422 / 0.9 = EUR 110,469), derived. Statutory: 19.5% including 6.98% health, on 90% of taxable individual-activity income, capped at 43 average wages (EUR 99,422). Business certificate holders pay 15.7% on the official minimum monthly salary. For individual activity with annual income up to EUR 42,500, a tax credit gives effective rates from 5% to 20% (KPMG); above that the main progressive rates apply.
income_tax.local_tax_note: There are no local, state or provincial personal income tax rates (PwC).

regimes.name: Individual activity credit (effective 5-20% income tax up to EUR 42,500)
regimes.description: Self-employed individual activity with annual income up to EUR 42,500 gets a tax credit that gives effective income tax rates from 5% to 20%; above that the main progressive rates apply. Social contributions at 19.5% on 90% of income, capped at EUR 99,422.
regimes.duration_note: Open-ended while income stays below EUR 42,500.

residence_routes: EU citizens may live and work freely. Non-EU nationals need a temporary residence permit for work or business; no remote-worker route was found and no official Lithuanian page was opened, so the details are unverified.
